title: Head repair III: LDA/Mahalanobis readout + class-balanced ridge at the sealed M297 lambda*
question: Do the LDA/Mahalanobis readout and the class-balanced ridge beat the sealed anchor 0.24214492753623187 with no feature change, at the train-side lambda M297 chose?

corpus.note: the sealed subsample parameters (the m109 _load_corpus digest gate)

artifacts.labels_note: the M142 cell-2 schedule labels - the ms codes are aligned to THIS order (the M228 discipline)

anchor.source: the sealed ms full-train penalty-1.0 aggregate (M228)

m298b_note: M298a VOIDED on g4: the eigen-vs-direct agreement at lambda=100 measured 6.96e-8 relative - exactly the fp64 floor for the comparison (eps * cond * sqrt(d) ~ 2.2e-16 * 2.9e7 * 115 ~ 7e-8); the registered 1e-8 was below the direct solve's conditioning resolution. M298b: agreement_tolerance 1e-8 -> 1e-6, registered before the re-run. The M298a grid finding stands on the record: all six LDA cells collapse to 1/345 regardless of lambda (the collapse is intrinsic to the mu_c-based readout at this feature scale, not the lambda transfer), so no readout is expected to improve the anchor.
m298a_note: run-1 (at lambda* = 30.0) sealed with gates PASS and H26-1 false: the LDA readout collapsed to a constant class (0.0029 = 1/345). Diagnosis measured BEFORE the amendment: a direct-space LDA collapses identically - the implementation matches its closed form; the registered transfer rule imported a scale mismatch (lambda* is a SOLVE regularization; at 30 it attenuates the readout's data term ~1/30 while the prior term is constant, so priors dominate). M298a: the LDA readout evaluates over its own registered grid; every cell validated by a direct-form agreement gate where the direct solve is meaningful (dropped == 0 and the direct solve's own residual <= 1e-8 - the 100.0 cell is the registered agreement anchor); H26-1 reads strictly on any cell. Run-1 evidence stays sealed (a valid negative cell, not a VOID).
registered_transfer_rule: lambda* is the M297 LOOCV choice, train-side only; it transfers to the LDA and balanced-ridge readouts as a registered constant. If M297 is not sealed, the cell is VOID (the fallback lambda is recorded but never feeds a solve when the dependency gate fails).

registered_readout_definitions.lda: scores x^T A^-1 m_c - 1/2 m_c^T A^-1 m_c + log(n_c/n), A = symmetric standardised Gram + lambda* I, m_c the class means
registered_readout_definitions.balanced_ridge: weighted least squares, per-row weight 1/n_{y_i} (each class contributes total weight 1), symmetric Gram + lambda* I, no prior term

interpretation_registered_before_running.g1_fail: VOID - row counts are a premise
interpretation_registered_before_running.g2_fail: VOID - the LU path must reproduce the sealed anchor or the instrument is not the sealed one
interpretation_registered_before_running.g3_fail: VOID - M298 cannot run before M297 seals lambda* and the eigendecomposition cache
interpretation_registered_before_running.g4_fail: VOID - a solve failed its backward instrument
interpretation_registered_before_running.any_readout_improves: H26-1 PASS: strict improvement over the anchor with no feature change
interpretation_registered_before_running.no_readout_improves: no readout beats the sealed anchor; H26-1 rests on the M297 ridge-at-star reading and on M299
